ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graphs of linear functions $y=kx$ and $y=-x+3$ are shown as in the figure. Then, what is the solution to the system of linear equations $\begin{cases}y=kx\\ y=-x+3\end{cases}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since the graph of the linear function $y=kx$ intersects with the graph of $y=-x+3$ at point $(1, 2)$,
therefore the solution to the system of linear equations $\begin{cases}y=kx\\ y=-x+3\end{cases}$ is $\boxed{\begin{cases}x=1\\ y=2\end{cases}}$.
